candidates.title: Edit by transcript: a text view where deleting words cuts the video, with retakes, fillers and pauses found for you
candidates.what: A Transcript tab (or window) shows the whole timeline as text in timeline order. The spoken word is highlighted during playback, and clicking a word moves the playhead there. Selecting a sentence and pressing Delete ripples that span out as one undo step. Cut words stay greyed in place and can be restored. A Retakes pass strikes through earlier takes of each repeated line, false starts, fillers and long pauses for review, and one click removes them all as one undo step. Words inside nests or transition overlaps show as not editable, with the reason. The jump-cut punch-in that creator-jobs bundled here is listed separately under C9.
proposed_by: differentiation (as a disqualifying gap, not a bet)
candidates.best_rationale: Rough-cutting A-roll is the largest time sink for every talking creator, and editing by transcript ships in every tool a creator compares against. Frame Job already has the inputs and outputs: per-media cached word timings (on-device SpeechTranscriber or AssemblyAI), detect_fillers, rc_project_source_map to map words through speed, reverse and ramps, and ripple_delete_ranges as one merged undo step that is already an MCP tool. So this is mostly a view, a mapping and a deterministic n-gram retake finder. No key and no format change are needed, because the transcript stays a per-media cache. Today a creator with 40 minutes of takes leaves for Descript or Gling at exactly this step, because cutting by transcript works only by asking the Assistant.
candidates.architecture_fit: Reads TranscriptReader/DeviceTranscriptCache/AssemblyAITranscript through get_transcript's per-media cache (AgentServer+Transcript.swift). Maps source words to timeline time per clip through source_window.rs and speed_map.rs (rc_project_source_map), the way Duck by Speech maps speech spans (audio_duck_speech.rs). Cuts go through ripple_delete_ranges (edit_time.rs), restore through the existing insert ops, and filler marks through detect_fillers. Adds a new inspector tab or window with a planned file split, a repetition finder, and an optional detect_retakes MCP tool. The view re-derives on every undo step.
claims_to_check: Code: Frame Job has no transcript view; cutting by transcript is possible only through the Assistant (get_transcript + ripple_delete_ranges).

Code: word timings are cached per media in source ticks (MediaTranscript.swift, DeviceTranscriptCache.swift, AssemblyAITranscript.swift) and served by get_transcript's cache (AgentServer+Transcript.swift).
Code: ripple_delete_ranges applies many ranges as ONE undo step and is an MCP tool.
Code: rc_project_source_map exists and maps source time to timeline time through speed, ramps and reverse.
Code: transcript-driven cuts (ripple_delete_ranges / detect_fillers) do not reach into nests or transition overlaps (spec §11 TR rules).
Code: on-device transcription keeps only about 1 in 8 fillers (spec §11 TR-7), and filler removal is cloud-only.
Code: a 4,096-clip cap exists in the core, and word-level cuts on a long recording could approach it.
Code: no repeated-take or false-start detector exists today.
Market: Descript, Screen Studio 4, Cap, Tella, Loom, Prequel, Gling and Premiere Paper Edit (26.5) all ship edit-by-transcript as of late 2026.
Market: 'editing and production is 21.4% of creator-channel comments, ahead of monetisation' has a citable source.

candidates.title: Screen recordings with the cursor as data: auto zoom, cursor polish and keystroke overlays
candidates.what: The recorder stops burning the pointer and clicks into the picture. It saves cursor position, cursor image, clicks and (opt-in) key events in a sidecar beside the movie. When the recording lands, zoom actions are already on the action lane at each click and typing burst. The cursor is a separate layer the creator can resize, restyle, smooth or hide when idle, with click ripples and sounds. Keycap overlays (the bundled Keyboard keys graphic) appear for every shortcut pressed, and typing stretches can be sped up with speed actions. Everything is an ordinary action, clip or graphic. Old recordings and imported screen videos behave as today. Camera layouts and wallpaper framing, which differentiation bundled here, are under C5.
candidates.best_rationale: Cursor data is the base of the whole polished-screencast category (Screen Studio, Cap, Prequel, FocuSee, Tella, Camtasia SmartFocus, ScreenKite), and Frame Job's recorder burns the cursor in and stores no events, so none of it can be built today. Frame Job loses its home segment to a $29/month subscription recorder. Leverage is high: add_zoom_action (edit_zoom.rs) already turns a rectangle into an eased zoom action, and the Keyboard keys template already takes a 'keys' prop, so auto zoom and keycaps are planners over existing ops. 'The free Screen Studio that is also a full editor and agent-drivable' is a press line no rival can claim. Screen Studio is subscription-only, OpenScreen's roughly 40k stars show the demand, and Cap's AGPL code can't be reused.
candidates.architecture_fit: Recorder: RecordingSetup.swift turns showsCursor and showMouseClicks off when cursor capture is on. It samples NSEvent.mouseLocation per frame, records clicks with a global NSEvent monitor, keys with a listen-only CGEvent tap (Input Monitoring grant in RecorderPanelController+Grants.swift) and the cursor image with NSCursor.currentSystem, and writes a sidecar per paused stretch, as the separate mic file is written. Core: a cursor source kind and recipe layer (recipe_layer.rs, format bump), smoothing and spring arithmetic in a new module, and auto-zoom and typing-speed-up planners that emit add_zoom_action and speed actions. Compositor: one more sprite layer. MCP: record_screen gains the option, plus an auto_zoom tool. The sidecar is not regenerable, so Consolidate and Relink must carry it.
competitor_refs: Screen Studio 4 auto zoom + cursor guide
Cap 0.6 auto zoom + keyboard overlay track
claims_to_check: Code: RecordingSetup.swift sets stream.showsCursor = true and stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks (spot-checked at lines 223-224 on 2026-11-01), so the cursor is burned into the movie.
Code: the recorder stores no cursor, click or key events anywhere.
Code: add_zoom_action (core edit_zoom.rs) turns a rectangle into an eased zoom action on the action lane.
Code: a bundled 'Keyboard keys' graphic template exists and takes a 'keys' prop.
Code: the compositor already draws image layers (a sprite), so a cursor layer needs a recipe_layer.rs kind and a format bump but no new compositor pass.
Code: issue #370 records timing or offset trouble in the recorder that event-to-frame alignment would inherit.
Code: Consolidate Media and Relink carry only the media file today (a sidecar would need adding).
Market: Screen Studio is subscription-only at about $29/month and withdrew its lifetime licence.
Market: OpenScreen has roughly 40k GitHub stars; Cap is AGPL-licensed.
Market: Cap, Tella and FocuSee ship keystroke overlays; Screen Studio, Cap, Prequel, FocuSee, Tella, Camtasia and ScreenKite ship click-driven auto zoom.

candidates.title: Vertical (9:16, 1:1) versions with on-device subject-tracking reframe that writes editable pans
candidates.what: Make a 9:16 or 1:1 version of a finished 16:9 edit. Each clip fills the frame and follows the face, person or salient region that Vision found on the Mac, or the cursor path from C2 in a screen recording, through ordinary eased x, y and scale actions the creator can nudge. Captions re-lay for the short side, graphics re-layout from the canvas size, and shots that can't be cropped get a blurred backdrop. The strategists disagree on the shape: a regenerated copy (creator-jobs, leverage) or linked versions in one project, where trimming the master updates every shape and one Export Queue entry renders all of them (differentiation).
candidates.best_rationale: Repurposing horizontal video into Shorts, Reels and TikToks is the most-wanted creator AI feature (Adobe Express: auto-repurposing 19%) and a weekly job for nearly every creator. Subject-tracking reframe is table stakes, and CapCut moved it behind Pro. Today set_canvas fits or letterboxes and every clip is repositioned by hand. Every piece except the analysis already exists: edit_fit.rs fill_scale, Add Blurred Background, word captions sized to the shorter side, and actions that ease x, y and scale. Tracking is offline analysis whose output is ordinary actions, so the one-pass compositor is untouched. That removes the reason spec §1 excluded auto-reframe. Linked versions would beat Premiere's drifting Auto Reframe Sequence copies. It is also the foundation for C6.
candidates.architecture_fit: Vision face, human and attention-saliency rectangles, sampled at about 5 fps (with VNTrackObjectRequest between detections), into a per-media analysis cache on MediaCacheLane. A dead-zone and ease planner in a new core module emits non-overlapping actions (edit_action.rs), on a wrapping nest (edit_nest.rs) where a clip already has actions. edit_canvas.rs gains a fill rescale mode. The copy path reuses Duplicate + set_canvas. Linked versions need a canvas per version, per-clip framing overrides keyed by clip id, a persisted field, a schema_vN and a format bump. Either path needs a spec §11 decision lifting the §1 auto-reframe non-goal before code. MCP: reframe_clip plus set_canvas's new mode.
candidates.effort: M (leverage, copy) to L (creator-jobs copy; differentiation linked versions)
competitor_refs: Premiere Auto Reframe / Auto Reframe Sequence
Final Cut Pro for iPad Auto Crop
Screen Studio vertical re-aim / Reel mode
claims_to_check: Code: set_canvas only fits or letterboxes existing clips on a canvas change; there is no fill rescale mode.
Code: a project has exactly one canvas, and a nest's canvas stays frozen at the size it was nested at.
Code: edit_fit.rs has a fill_scale, and an Add Blurred Background command exists.
Code: word captions size to the canvas's shorter side, and graphic modules receive the canvas size.
Code: the app imports no Vision framework today (spot-check found no `import Vision` in app/Sources).
Code: a clip cannot carry overlapping actions of the same kind (the rule a reframe planner must avoid).
Code: spec §1 (designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md) lists auto-reframe as a non-goal.

Market: Adobe Express's creator survey puts auto-repurposing at 19%, the most-wanted AI feature.
Market: OpusClip, Premiere, Final Cut Pro (iPad Auto Crop), Riverside and Screen Studio all ship reframe, and each produces a separate copy rather than a linked version.

candidates.title: Podcast and interview: switch angles by who is talking, and read every audio track of a file
candidates.what: Stack one track per camera (or a multicam clip), aligned by Synchronize Audio, and choose Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking, using each mic's speech spans judged against that mic's own floor. It uses the wide shot during crosstalk, holds a minimum shot length, and can add reaction shots. The result is one undo step, every cut stays an ordinary split the creator can roll or re-pick, and it is an MCP tool. As a prerequisite, OBS, Zoom and multitrack-recorder files import with every audio track instead of only the first. Differentiation adds a multicam clip with an angle grid and live 1–4 overrides during playback; the other two angles defer that.
candidates.best_rationale: Switching angles by hand is the video podcaster's longest chore, and video podcasts are the fastest-growing segment (YouTube reports over 1B monthly podcast viewers). The alternatives are paid or partial: AutoPod at about $29/month, Resolve SmartSwitch only in Studio, metered Descript and Eddie. Frame Job already has the hard audio half no plugin has: drift-corrected sync, cached Silero speech spans, the 10 ms loudness cache, Match Audio, Enhance Voice and the leveller. So the switcher is a planner over cached data that emits existing ops. Fixing the first-audio-track limit also stops silently losing the second mic.
candidates.architecture_fit: The switch is a new core op (e.g. edit_angles.rs) composing split + set_enabled on inactive angles as ONE undo step, the way insert_clip composes split + insert time. Inputs are media_speech.rs/SileroVAD.swift spans and ClipLoudness.swift, plus optional Vision mouth activity for one-mic shows. Reading every audio track means CompositionBuilder.firstTrack and core container.rs gain an audio-track index on the media or clip (format bump), with one linked clip per track at import. Split-screen comes from C5's layouts. Lifting the spec §1 multicam non-goal needs a §11 decision: narrowly for stacked tracks, or fully for a multicam clip as a nest with an angle-cut lane.
candidates.effort: M (creator-jobs, leverage: stacked tracks) to L (differentiation: multicam clip + angle grid)
competitor_refs: Riverside Editor agent layouts / in-person multicam
Final Cut Pro for iPad Live Multicam

Code: Synchronize Audio lands its alignment as move_clip and set_speed, with drift correction.
Code: Silero speech spans are cached per media (core media_speech.rs, SileroVAD.swift) and can be read per clip (audio_duck_speech.rs).
Code: plan.rs has MAX_CONCURRENT_VIDEO_TRACKS = 8 (spot-checked); check whether exceeding it only warns, and whether a disabled (set_enabled off) clip still decodes.
Code: no existing op composes split + set_enabled across tracks as a single undo step.
Code: a 2-hour, 3-angle episode cut every ~8 s (~2,700 clips) would fit under, but approach, the 4,096-clip cap.
Code: spec §1 lists multicam as a non-goal.
Market: AutoPod costs about $29/month; Resolve SmartSwitch is Studio-only.
Market: YouTube reports over 1B monthly podcast viewers; Spotify says over 500M users have streamed a video podcast.

candidates.title: Camera cutout without a green screen, and camera layouts that switch mid-video
candidates.what: Tick Cut Out Person (or Remove Background) on a camera clip, and Vision segments the person on the Mac, rendered in the background like Reverse. Text Behind Subject places a title between the person and their background, using a duplicate clip with cutout on. A Layout pop-up switches the camera at the playhead, with an animated move, between corner bubble (circle or rounded), side by side, stacked for vertical, camera full and screen only. It can also frame a padded wallpaper and a rounded, shadowed window, and 'Hide camera while silent' fades the camera out during pauses using cached speech spans. Brings #124 out of the icebox.

The mask is rendered to an 8-bit gray HEVC (or an alpha copy) in cache/masks/ through the ReverseRenderer/ReverseCache/BackgroundRender/MediaCacheLedger pattern. Layouts are an action preset in the motion-presets family. Hide-while-silent uses speech_in_clip and writes opacity actions. MCP: set_video's cutout key plus a camera_layout tool. The mask timing must follow speed changes and ramps, and HLG projects need the matte in the right working space.

candidates.title: Find Clips: ranked moments from a long video that open as real vertical edits
candidates.what: Clip ▸ Find Clips… on an episode, VOD or finished edit lists 10–30 candidates of 20–60 s. Each has in and out points snapped to sentence ends, a length, a one-line reason ('laughter after the punchline', 'the clearest statement of the thesis') and a preview, with no virality score. Make Short turns checked candidates into vertical projects or versions: reframed (C3), word-captioned, cleaned of fillers, with a hook title, queued for export. Each can be reviewed as a Proposal (C12) before it lands. Ranking runs on the user's Claude key, or (per leverage and differentiation) on-device FoundationModels per chunk, with an on-device signal-only fallback when there is no key.
candidates.best_rationale: Long-to-short is what OpusClip (16M+ users), Riverside Magic Clips, Submagic, Descript Clips and Kapwing win on, all metered by credits, and Frame Job has nothing here. Cost is the biggest barrier to AI adoption (38%). Frame Job can do it locally. The cached transcript gives sentence boundaries, which answers the main Magic Clips complaint about cuts in the wrong place. The 10 ms loudness cache gives energy. Sound Analysis adds the non-verbal moments (laughter, applause, cheering) that transcript-only clippers miss. Every candidate opens as a real timeline instead of a black-box render, and every step is an MCP tool, so outside agents run the same job.
candidates.architecture_fit: SNClassifySoundRequest(.version1) on MediaCacheLane into a per-media label cache, ClipLoudness.swift peaks, and get_transcript sentence spans. Ranking is an Assistant recipe (AssistantPrompt.swift) over chunked transcripts with cached results, or a FoundationModels pass. Candidates set_range; Make Short copies the range into new_project, then set_canvas vertical, C3's reframe, detect_fillers + ripple_delete_ranges, and the existing caption pipeline. MCP: find_clips answers the ranked list. It depends on C3 and on C1's word-to-timeline mapping, and in differentiation's version also on C12 and C13.
claims_to_check: Code: no moment-finding or clip-candidate feature exists today.

candidates.title: Publish kit: platform presets with rule checks, safe zones, chapter text, drafted titles and thumbnails
candidates.what: Export (or File ▸ Prepare for Publishing / Publish Kit) offers named targets: YouTube, YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Reels, Spotify video podcast and Apple Podcasts. Each sets size, codec and loudness and checks the project against that platform's published rules, with one-click fixes. View ▸ Safe Zones overlays the platform UI (labelled approximate). A Publish panel gives a copyable '00:00 Intro' chapter list built from chapter markers and checked against YouTube's rule. It drafts titles, a description and chapter names from the transcript, on-device with FoundationModels (no key) or with the user's Claude key. It also offers a thumbnail picker: suggested frames scored by Vision aesthetics, 1280×720, with a title-graphic template and three variants. Translated subtitles, which differentiation bundles here, are under C11.
candidates.best_rationale: It hits every creator on every upload and closes four inventory gaps in roughly one phase that is mostly formatting and wiring: platform presets, safe zones, chapter text, and title and description drafts. The platform rules (YouTube chapters: 00:00 first, at least 3, each at least 10 s; Spotify's video spec; Apple Podcasts loudness) are exact enough to check deterministically, which makes 'Frame Job won't let you ship a broken upload' a true claim. FoundationModels drafts give an AI tier with no key and no cost that no hosted rival can offer. Its value comes from frequency rather than from removing a hard give-up point.
candidates.architecture_fit: Presets are data rows in core export_preset.rs and ExportPresetsStore.swift. Rule checks are pure core validators kept as data with an as-of date. Chapter text is a read of add_marker {chapter} markers, the same source ExporterWriter+Chapters.swift embeds. Safe zones extend the existing 90/80% safe-area guide drawing. Drafts are a FoundationModels LanguageModelSession with @Generable output, chunked for its ~4k context, or an Assistant recipe over get_transcript. Thumbnails use Vision CalculateImageAestheticsScoresRequest feeding the existing Save Frame…, plus a bundled graphic template. MCP: a publish_kit read tool. An HLG project exported for Spotify needs the SDR version.
competitor_refs: Tella social safe zones + direct publishing
YouTube Studio chapters and three-thumbnail test

candidates.title: Caption design and saved styles, with a brand kit and project templates
candidates.what: Captions: an inspector Captions section exposes every word-style colour, size, background and animation as a control (today some are set only by an agent). Keyword emphasis lets the creator mark words, or have names and numbers picked by NLTagger or the Assistant, to show bigger in a highlight colour. An emoji can follow chosen words. Any caption setup or text look saves as a named style. Brand kit: brand colours and fonts appear first in every colour well and font menu and feed graphic templates' colour props by default. Templates: save a project as a template with intro, outro, logo bug, lower third, caption style and export preset, then File ▸ New from Template. Creator-jobs proposed captions and brand kit as two bets; leverage proposed them as one, and differentiation listed 'saved text and caption styles and brand colours' as one gap.

Final Cut Pro iPad Creator Themes

candidates.title: Hide jump cuts: deterministic punch-in, optional interpolated smooth cuts, and optical-flow slow motion
candidates.what: After transcript cuts, Remove Silences or filler removal, 'Punch in on cuts' alternates a gentle scale (100% ↔ about 112%) across cuts within one continuous take, centred on the face. These are ordinary scale and position values, free and exact, with no generated frames (creator-jobs, differentiation). Leverage adds Smooth All Cuts: a short VideoToolbox-interpolated morph at each abutting cut, as a new 'smooth' transition kind, rendered in the background like Reverse. The same renderer gives a clip at ×0.25 interpolated frames instead of repeated ones, plus source motion blur for sped-up shots. Slow motion is separable from cut smoothing; the two are grouped only because they share a renderer.
proposed_by: leverage (interpolated smooth cuts and slow motion)
candidates.best_rationale: Every cleanup feature (C1, filler removal, Remove Silences) leaves jump cuts, and smoothed jump cuts are a named table-stakes gap. Descript 'Smooth all' (billed per second) and Riverside Smooth cuts shipped in 2026. A deterministic punch-in is the human editor's trick, needs no disclosure and stays editable. VTFrameProcessor (VTFrameRateConversionConfiguration, VTMotionBlurConfiguration, macOS 15.4+) makes interpolation and optical-flow retiming an offline render in the existing derived-media pipeline, which removes the reason spec §1 excluded optical-flow retiming.
candidates.architecture_fit: Punch-in is a pure core rule over cut points (adjacent cuts in the same media) writing set_clip scale and position, with face centre from Vision (C3 or C13's analysis). Interpolation follows ReverseRenderer.swift/ReverseCache.swift, writing cache/interpolated/ and cache/smooth-cuts/ through BackgroundRender. Slow motion: set_speed below ×1 opts into the interpolated copy through a video key (format bump), read by the plan as a reversed copy is. Smooth cuts: a 'smooth' kind in transition.rs/edit_transition_style.rs, valid only at an abutting cut. MCP: set_transition_style's kind plus a smooth_cuts tool. A spike must first confirm 10-bit/HLG support in VTFrameProcessor. Ramps are excluded at first.
claims_to_check: Code: set_clip scale and position can be written per clip with no new op, so a punch-in pass needs only a planner.
Code: a clip slowed below ×1 repeats frames today (no interpolation).
Code: transition kinds live in core transition.rs/edit_transition_style.rs, and there is no 'smooth' kind.
Code: the reversed-media render pattern (ReverseRenderer/ReverseCache/BackgroundRender) can host another derived video file per media.
Code: spec §1 lists optical-flow retiming and motion blur as non-goals.
Tech: VTFrameProcessor's VTFrameRateConversionConfiguration and VTMotionBlurConfiguration exist on macOS 15.4+, support up to 8192×4320, and whether they accept 10-bit/HLG pixel formats (unverified).
Market: Descript 'Smooth all' is billed per second and generates frames; Riverside shipped Smooth cuts in 2026.

candidates.title: Footage you can skim: a source viewer, In/Out placement, favourite ranges and proxies
candidates.what: Double-click a file in the Media tab to open it in a source viewer. Skim by hovering, mark In and Out (or save favourite ranges), and drop only that range on the timeline. add_clip (and insert or overwrite) gains a source range. 4K and multi-hour files get a half-size proxy built in the background, used only by playback and never by export or render_frame. Differentiation adds measuring 4K and multi-hour playback first, with proxies if it falls short. Creator-jobs bundles proxies with the viewer; differentiation lists source ranges and proxies as two separate gaps.
proposed_by: differentiation (as disqualifying gaps; source range also inside its footage-index bet)
candidates.best_rationale: Today a placed clip is always the whole file, the browser has no skimming, there are no proxies, and performance has been measured only at 1080p. The vlog and stream workflows stop here, and every NLE a creator graduates to has a source monitor and proxies. Placing a range is also what C13's search hits and C6's candidates need. Differentiation calls an unmeasured 4K and multi-hour playback figure, with no proxies, the biggest single risk to any 'leading' claim, and a likely prerequisite for C4 at 3–4 angles.
candidates.architecture_fit: Placements already carry a source offset (trim, slip). The op change is add_clip/insert/overwrite taking a source range in op_table.rs, printed into the MCP tools automatically by AgentCatalog.opTool. Favourite ranges are media-level ranges in source ticks, like speech spans. The source viewer is a Swift view. Proxies are a half-size render into the package cache (the reversed render's pattern), swapped in only by the playback CompositionBuilder. This settles #112. It runs against the owner's 'features before performance' order unless proxies are framed as a feature.
candidates.effort: M (source ranges + viewer) to L (with proxies)

candidates.title: Captions in every language, translated on the Mac, with soft subtitle tracks
candidates.what: After generating captions, tick target languages (Spanish, German, Japanese…) and get a translated caption track for each, translated on-device by Apple's Translation framework. Whole sentences are translated and then re-paged. Export an SRT or WebVTT per language, or one MP4/MOV (and WebM) with every language as a selectable soft subtitle track. candidates.title: Proposals and Recipes: play the agent's cut before it lands, and one-click open creator workflows
candidates.what: Proposals: a multi-step edit from the Assistant or any MCP agent builds a side chain of handles plus its edit log. The timeline shows it as a diff (added clips ghosted, removed spans struck through, changed clips badged), Space plays the proposed version, and an A/B key toggles it with the current cut. Accept applies it as one named undo step, or step by step. If the creator edited in the meantime, the log replays and names any step now refused in the rule's own sentence. Recipes: a Recipes menu in the Assistant tab ('Tighten a talking head', 'Podcast episode → 6 vertical clips', 'Chapters and description'), each showing its estimated cost on the creator's key first and landing as a Proposal. The same recipes are served as MCP prompts by framejob-mcp (so Claude subscription users need no API key), and anyone can share them as .fjrecipe files. Recipes depend on Proposals; Proposals stand alone.
candidates.best_rationale: In 2026 every tool has an agent and an MCP server; what separates them is trust. Adobe's 2026 survey found 44% of creators want to review, edit or undo an agent's work and 37% want to see what it is doing. Rivals approve a text plan, but only an editor whose project is an immutable value and whose edits are pure, refusable ops can play the whole result before applying it. It also fixes a documented limit: a ten-edit turn takes ten Undos. Recipes make the agent-native story visible without prompt-writing and give press a one-click demo, open and priced up front, against CapCut's closed, credit-billed Skills Marketplace.
candidates.architecture_fit: Handles are immutable and ProjectDocument is the single mutation point, so a proposal is a side chain of handles plus a log, and the composition builder already builds from any handle. New: an rc_project_diff export (Rust → header → ReelCore.swift) diffing by clip id, a `proposal` envelope key beside `scope`, and open/accept/discard tools with catalog and parity rows. Replay uses the same apply path, so refusals come for free. Recipes are data (brief, allowed tools, checks) with no runtime, inside spec §11 R5-1/G-1. mcp-proxy gains prompts/list. The startup parity check tests each recipe's tool list. Cost estimates come from agent/src/pricing.ts.

ScreenKite (confirm:false then confirm:true; agent tools on the user's own plan)

candidates.title: Ask your footage: an on-device media index that creators and agents can search
candidates.what: Every imported file is analysed in the background: spoken words (Speech), shot changes, faces and people (Vision), on-screen text (Vision text recognition), sounds such as laughter, applause, music and typing (Sound Analysis), and loudness peaks. Media-tab search finds 'where I open Settings', 'laughter' or 'the dog' and returns ranges to drop on the timeline. Agents query the same index through a search_media tool. It is the shared analysis layer that C3 (faces), C6 (moments), C9 (face centre) and C4 (mouth activity) would otherwise each build narrowly; creator-jobs and leverage propose only the Sound Analysis slice, inside the clip finder.
candidates.best_rationale: Final Cut Pro 12 Visual and Transcript Search, Resolve IntelliSearch (Studio only) and Premiere Media Intelligence all shipped within a year, but none exposes the index to an agent. OpusClip, Kapwing and CapCut sell moment-finding per credit in the cloud. A local index that both the creator and any agent can query costs nothing per minute and becomes the foundation for shorts, reframe, multicam and presenter features.
candidates.architecture_fit: Follows the existing per-media caches (sound caches, get_transcript's on-device cache). Swift owns the ML calls; Rust can own the index format (versioned) and queries. Placing a hit needs add_clip to take a source range (C10). Analysis samples a few frames a second and runs on AC or when idle.

candidates.title: Script to cut: a teleprompter that listens, and takes assembled from the script
candidates.what: Paste a script into the recorder. A teleprompter beside the camera scrolls with the creator's voice using on-device live speech recognition, pauses when they go off script, and marks which line each take covered. When they stop, Assemble builds a Proposal: the best complete take of each line (fewest fillers, no stumble, last take by default) in script order, retakes removed, and captions taken from the script's own spelling. The same alignment works on imported footage that has a transcript.
candidates.best_rationale: For educators, time is the main barrier to making their own videos (NUS 2025). Resolve IntelliScript and Premiere Paper Edit assemble from a script but have no recorder, while Prequel, Cap and Loom have teleprompters but no assembly. Frame Job owns both the recorder and the transcript tools, so it knows the script before the footage exists and can close the loop end to end on-device.
candidates.architecture_fit: The recorder panel and camera stack get a teleprompter window. SpeechEngine/Transcriber (SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber) do on-device recognition. The script becomes a project field (format bump). Script-to-word alignment is pure Rust sequence alignment. Assembly is ordinary ops in a Proposal (C12), and it overlaps C1's retake detection.

claims_to_check: Code: SpeechEngine.swift uses SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber and can run live (streaming) recognition during a recording.

Market: Resolve IntelliScript and Premiere Paper Edit assemble from a script but include no recorder.

do_not_chase.item: Generative media: AI B-roll and video generation, avatars and AI twins, voice cloning and overdub, lip-synced dubbing
do_not_chase.reason: Nothing on-device can do it, so it means brokering credit-metered vendor APIs and several keys with constant model churn. That is the business model Frame Job competes against. It carries disclosure, authenticity and demonetisation risk (YouTube's synthetic-content rule, TikTok C2PA labels), and YouTube (27 languages) and Instagram (14) now dub for free. The cheap localisation path is on-device translated subtitles (C11).

do_not_chase.item: Direct upload and scheduling, hosted share links, platform analytics
do_not_chase.reason: An open-source app with no backend can't keep OAuth client secrets. YouTube's upload scope needs app verification, and its per-project quota would cap all users together at a few uploads a day. Uploads from unaudited projects are locked private, and TikTok and Meta posting APIs need audits. Share links need a server, and the platforms own the analytics. Export per platform and copy chapters and descriptions (C7) instead. Share links could come later only as bring-your-own storage.

do_not_chase.item: Stock music, SFX and B-roll libraries, or a template marketplace / template-volume race
do_not_chase.reason: It needs licensing, curation, bandwidth and a backend, and a solo developer can't match the network effects (CapCut's 400,000+ templates a day, MotionVFX inside Final Cut Pro, Epidemic Sound in VEED). The counter already exists: agent-written graphics and shareable .fjgraphic packages.

do_not_chase.item: Eye-contact correction and face retouching (reshape, de-age, beauty)
do_not_chase.reason: Apple has no public gaze or face-reshape API for recorded video, so it would need cloud or custom generative face models with uncanny failure modes, likeness risk and a per-frame cost that doesn't fit the one-pass compositor. None of the creator workflows breaks here.

do_not_chase.item: Cloud sync, real-time collaboration, mobile or iPad companion apps, Windows
do_not_chase.reason: Each needs a backend or a second platform, and each is off the local, open, Mac-only thesis.

do_not_chase.item: Remote guest recording and live multi-camera capture
do_not_chase.reason: That is Riverside's moat and needs WebRTC servers. Import the per-guest tracks Riverside, Zoom and StreamYard already produce, and switch between them with C4.

do_not_chase.item: A virality score on found clips
do_not_chase.reason: Reviewers discard many of OpusClip's scored clips, and a number invites distrust. A stated reason per moment is honest and controllable. Differentiation's and leverage's clip bets also present reasons rather than scores.

do_not_chase.item: Stabilisation, for now
do_not_chase.reason: Phones stabilise in camera, and it mainly serves handheld vlogs, not the talking-head, screencast and podcast segments where Frame Job wins. Leverage notes it is feasible later (Vision homographic registration into a cached copy, about M). Differentiation adds that Resolve and Final Cut Pro already own it as pro finishing.

do_not_chase.item: Live-compositor motion blur
do_not_chase.reason: Blur on animated layers needs N sub-frame passes, which breaks the one-pass compositor. At most it becomes export-only sub-frame accumulation later. Source-footage blur can come offline from VTMotionBlur (C9). Differentiation notes rivals put motion blur on zooms, as a C2 risk.

do_not_chase.item: Optical-flow slow motion / retiming (CONTESTED: leverage proposes it in C9)
do_not_chase.reason: Creator-jobs: heavy pixel work, and the vlog workflow breaks earlier, at footage handling. Differentiation: pro finishing that Resolve and Final Cut Pro own, and not a differentiator for creators. Leverage disagrees: VTFrameProcessor makes it an offline render in the existing Reverse pipeline.

do_not_chase.item: A full multicam clip with an angle viewer as a first move (CONTESTED: differentiation proposes it in C4)
do_not_chase.reason: It strains the 8-decoder budget in plan.rs with no proxies. Speaker switching on stacked synced tracks gets most of the value first, and creator-jobs says no angle viewer is needed.

do_not_chase.item: A plugin system: third-party effects, user shaders, Audio Unit hosting
do_not_chase.reason: It contradicts the closed, versioned effect vocabulary (spec §11 R5-1, G-1) behind deterministic preview/export parity and the proof suite, which is the property that makes agent editing trustworthy. JS graphic modules stay the one extension point.

do_not_chase.item: More MCP surface or a second agent mode as the headline (CONTESTED: differentiation makes Proposals and Recipes its first bets)
do_not_chase.reason: MCP became table stakes in 2026 (Descript, Kapwing, OpusClip, Tella, Resolve 21.1), and Frame Job's whole-editor depth is already ahead. Each creator job shipped as ops becomes an agent tool for free. Differentiation agrees that MCP alone no longer differentiates.

do_not_chase.item: Pro finishing as headline features: Dolby Vision, synthetic depth of field
do_not_chase.reason: Resolve and Final Cut Pro already own these, they cost compositor work, the owner has closed several colour items, and Frame Job's colour and HDR is already ahead of every creator tool.

do_not_chase.item: Analytics-driven idea and trend features
do_not_chase.reason: The platforms hold the performance data (Edits Assistant, YouTube A/B tests), and it doesn't play to the local, agent-driven NLE advantage.

disagreements: What comes first. Differentiation leads with agent trust and packaging: Proposals and Recipes (C12), then the on-device index (C13), then the workflows. Creator-jobs puts 'more MCP surface or a second agent mode as the headline' in do_not_chase and spends road maps on creator jobs, led by transcript editing and vertical reframe. Leverage leads with the cheapest high-value items: transcript, cursor-as-data, and the S-size publish kit.

Vertical reframe shape (C3). Creator-jobs and leverage make a regenerated 9:16 copy (Duplicate + set_canvas + reframe). Leverage calls a linked 16:9/9:16 pair a much larger L. Differentiation insists on linked versions in one project (a canvas per version and per-clip framing overrides), because every competitor's copy drifts from the master. Creator-jobs flags this as a decision to make early.

Multicam scope (C4). Creator-jobs and leverage want 'multicam-lite' on stacked synced tracks with no angle viewer, and leverage puts the full multicam clip in do_not_chase until proxies exist. Differentiation proposes a multicam clip with an angle grid and live 1–4 overrides (L), and says measuring decode first may make proxies a prerequisite.

Jump cuts (C9). Differentiation argues for a deterministic punch-in precisely because Descript's and Riverside's smoothing generates frames, with a cost and a disclosure question. Leverage proposes VTFrameProcessor interpolated morphs, arguing optical flow is not generative. Creator-jobs and differentiation both list optical-flow retiming or slow motion as not to chase, while leverage lifts that non-goal now.

Effort estimates diverge. Transcript editing: M (leverage) vs L (creator-jobs). Cursor-as-data: M (leverage) vs L (creator-jobs, differentiation). Vertical reframe: M (leverage) vs L (others). Podcast switching: M (creator-jobs, leverage) vs L (differentiation). Publish kit: S (leverage) vs M (others).

Proxies and performance (C10). Differentiation names an unmeasured 4K/multi-hour playback figure as the biggest risk to any 'leading' claim, and a disqualifying gap. Creator-jobs bundles proxies into the source viewer and frames them as a feature to get past the owner's 'features before performance' order. Leverage proposes no proxy work and defers anything that needs them.

On-device language model. Differentiation and leverage both use Apple FoundationModels for no-key drafts and ranking (titles, chapters, clip ranking per chunk). Creator-jobs uses only the user's Claude key, with a signal-only on-device fallback (loudness, laughter, sentence boundaries) when there is no key.

Cutout implementation (C5). Creator-jobs renders a person-alpha copy of the clip and plays it. Differentiation renders a matte movie placed through the existing matte-track roles, with no compositor change. Leverage offers the matte track as a no-format-change first phase, then a per-layer mask texture and a video.cutout key (format bump).

Translation. Leverage makes on-device translated captions and soft subtitle tracks its own bet (C11). Differentiation folds them into the publish bet. Creator-jobs mentions translated subtitles only in passing, as the cheap localisation alternative to dubbing.

How retakes are found. Creator-jobs and leverage use deterministic sentence or n-gram similarity over cached words (C1). Differentiation also proposes script-driven take selection by aligning takes to a pasted script (C14), which needs live recognition and a script field.

Analysis layer. Differentiation builds one shared, versioned on-device footage index (C13, L) as the foundation for shorts, reframe, multicam and presenter features. Creator-jobs and leverage add only the narrow per-feature caches each bet needs (Vision face boxes for reframe, Sound Analysis labels for the clip finder).

candidates.title: Edit by transcript: a text view where deleting words cuts the video, with retakes, fillers and pauses found for you
candidates.what: A Transcript tab (or window) shows the whole timeline as text in timeline order. The spoken word is highlighted during playback, and clicking a word moves the playhead there. Selecting a sentence and pressing Delete ripples that span out as one undo step. Cut words stay greyed in place and can be restored. A Retakes pass strikes through earlier takes of each repeated line, false starts, fillers and long pauses for review, and one click removes them all as one undo step. Words inside nests or transition overlaps show as not editable, with the reason. The jump-cut punch-in that creator-jobs bundled here is listed separately under C9.
proposed_by: differentiation (as a disqualifying gap, not a bet)
candidates.best_rationale: Rough-cutting A-roll is the largest time sink for every talking creator, and editing by transcript ships in every tool a creator compares against. Frame Job already has the inputs and outputs: per-media cached word timings (on-device SpeechTranscriber or AssemblyAI), detect_fillers, rc_project_source_map to map words through speed, reverse and ramps, and ripple_delete_ranges as one merged undo step that is already an MCP tool. So this is mostly a view, a mapping and a deterministic n-gram retake finder. No key and no format change are needed, because the transcript stays a per-media cache. Today a creator with 40 minutes of takes leaves for Descript or Gling at exactly this step, because cutting by transcript works only by asking the Assistant.
candidates.architecture_fit: Reads TranscriptReader/DeviceTranscriptCache/AssemblyAITranscript through get_transcript's per-media cache (AgentServer+Transcript.swift). Maps source words to timeline time per clip through source_window.rs and speed_map.rs (rc_project_source_map), the way Duck by Speech maps speech spans (audio_duck_speech.rs). Cuts go through ripple_delete_ranges (edit_time.rs), restore through the existing insert ops, and filler marks through detect_fillers. Adds a new inspector tab or window with a planned file split, a repetition finder, and an optional detect_retakes MCP tool. The view re-derives on every undo step.
claims_to_check: Code: Frame Job has no transcript view; cutting by transcript is possible only through the Assistant (get_transcript + ripple_delete_ranges).

Code: word timings are cached per media in source ticks (MediaTranscript.swift, DeviceTranscriptCache.swift, AssemblyAITranscript.swift) and served by get_transcript's cache (AgentServer+Transcript.swift).
Code: ripple_delete_ranges applies many ranges as ONE undo step and is an MCP tool.
Code: rc_project_source_map exists and maps source time to timeline time through speed, ramps and reverse.
Code: transcript-driven cuts (ripple_delete_ranges / detect_fillers) do not reach into nests or transition overlaps (spec §11 TR rules).
Code: on-device transcription keeps only about 1 in 8 fillers (spec §11 TR-7), and filler removal is cloud-only.
Code: a 4,096-clip cap exists in the core, and word-level cuts on a long recording could approach it.
Code: no repeated-take or false-start detector exists today.
Market: Descript, Screen Studio 4, Cap, Tella, Loom, Prequel, Gling and Premiere Paper Edit (26.5) all ship edit-by-transcript as of late 2026.
Market: 'editing and production is 21.4% of creator-channel comments, ahead of monetisation' has a citable source.

candidates.title: Screen recordings with the cursor as data: auto zoom, cursor polish and keystroke overlays
candidates.what: The recorder stops burning the pointer and clicks into the picture. It saves cursor position, cursor image, clicks and (opt-in) key events in a sidecar beside the movie. When the recording lands, zoom actions are already on the action lane at each click and typing burst. The cursor is a separate layer the creator can resize, restyle, smooth or hide when idle, with click ripples and sounds. Keycap overlays (the bundled Keyboard keys graphic) appear for every shortcut pressed, and typing stretches can be sped up with speed actions. Everything is an ordinary action, clip or graphic. Old recordings and imported screen videos behave as today. Camera layouts and wallpaper framing, which differentiation bundled here, are under C5.
candidates.best_rationale: Cursor data is the base of the whole polished-screencast category (Screen Studio, Cap, Prequel, FocuSee, Tella, Camtasia SmartFocus, ScreenKite), and Frame Job's recorder burns the cursor in and stores no events, so none of it can be built today. Frame Job loses its home segment to a $29/month subscription recorder. Leverage is high: add_zoom_action (edit_zoom.rs) already turns a rectangle into an eased zoom action, and the Keyboard keys template already takes a 'keys' prop, so auto zoom and keycaps are planners over existing ops. 'The free Screen Studio that is also a full editor and agent-drivable' is a press line no rival can claim. Screen Studio is subscription-only, OpenScreen's roughly 40k stars show the demand, and Cap's AGPL code can't be reused.
candidates.architecture_fit: Recorder: RecordingSetup.swift turns showsCursor and showMouseClicks off when cursor capture is on. It samples NSEvent.mouseLocation per frame, records clicks with a global NSEvent monitor, keys with a listen-only CGEvent tap (Input Monitoring grant in RecorderPanelController+Grants.swift) and the cursor image with NSCursor.currentSystem, and writes a sidecar per paused stretch, as the separate mic file is written. Core: a cursor source kind and recipe layer (recipe_layer.rs, format bump), smoothing and spring arithmetic in a new module, and auto-zoom and typing-speed-up planners that emit add_zoom_action and speed actions. Compositor: one more sprite layer. MCP: record_screen gains the option, plus an auto_zoom tool. The sidecar is not regenerable, so Consolidate and Relink must carry it.
competitor_refs: Screen Studio 4 auto zoom + cursor guide
Cap 0.6 auto zoom + keyboard overlay track

Code: add_zoom_action (core edit_zoom.rs) turns a rectangle into an eased zoom action on the action lane.

Code: the compositor already draws image layers (a sprite), so a cursor layer needs a recipe_layer.rs kind and a format bump but no new compositor pass.

Code: Consolidate Media and Relink carry only the media file today (a sidecar would need adding).

candidates.title: Vertical (9:16, 1:1) versions with on-device subject-tracking reframe that writes editable pans
candidates.what: Make a 9:16 or 1:1 version of a finished 16:9 edit. Each clip fills the frame and follows the face, person or salient region that Vision found on the Mac, or the cursor path from C2 in a screen recording, through ordinary eased x, y and scale actions the creator can nudge. Captions re-lay for the short side, graphics re-layout from the canvas size, and shots that can't be cropped get a blurred backdrop. The strategists disagree on the shape: a regenerated copy (creator-jobs, leverage) or linked versions in one project, where trimming the master updates every shape and one Export Queue entry renders all of them (differentiation).
candidates.best_rationale: Repurposing horizontal video into Shorts, Reels and TikToks is the most-wanted creator AI feature (Adobe Express: auto-repurposing 19%) and a weekly job for nearly every creator. Subject-tracking reframe is table stakes, and CapCut moved it behind Pro. Today set_canvas fits or letterboxes and every clip is repositioned by hand. Every piece except the analysis already exists: edit_fit.rs fill_scale, Add Blurred Background, word captions sized to the shorter side, and actions that ease x, y and scale. Tracking is offline analysis whose output is ordinary actions, so the one-pass compositor is untouched. That removes the reason spec §1 excluded auto-reframe. Linked versions would beat Premiere's drifting Auto Reframe Sequence copies. It is also the foundation for C6.
candidates.architecture_fit: Vision face, human and attention-saliency rectangles, sampled at about 5 fps (with VNTrackObjectRequest between detections), into a per-media analysis cache on MediaCacheLane. A dead-zone and ease planner in a new core module emits non-overlapping actions (edit_action.rs), on a wrapping nest (edit_nest.rs) where a clip already has actions. edit_canvas.rs gains a fill rescale mode. The copy path reuses Duplicate + set_canvas. Linked versions need a canvas per version, per-clip framing overrides keyed by clip id, a persisted field, a schema_vN and a format bump. Either path needs a spec §11 decision lifting the §1 auto-reframe non-goal before code. MCP: reframe_clip plus set_canvas's new mode.
candidates.effort: M (leverage, copy) to L (creator-jobs copy; differentiation linked versions)
competitor_refs: Premiere Auto Reframe / Auto Reframe Sequence
Final Cut Pro for iPad Auto Crop
Screen Studio vertical re-aim / Reel mode

candidates.title: Podcast and interview: switch angles by who is talking, and read every audio track of a file
candidates.what: Stack one track per camera (or a multicam clip), aligned by Synchronize Audio, and choose Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking, using each mic's speech spans judged against that mic's own floor. It uses the wide shot during crosstalk, holds a minimum shot length, and can add reaction shots. The result is one undo step, every cut stays an ordinary split the creator can roll or re-pick, and it is an MCP tool. As a prerequisite, OBS, Zoom and multitrack-recorder files import with every audio track instead of only the first. Differentiation adds a multicam clip with an angle grid and live 1–4 overrides during playback; the other two angles defer that.
candidates.best_rationale: Switching angles by hand is the video podcaster's longest chore, and video podcasts are the fastest-growing segment (YouTube reports over 1B monthly podcast viewers). The alternatives are paid or partial: AutoPod at about $29/month, Resolve SmartSwitch only in Studio, metered Descript and Eddie. Frame Job already has the hard audio half no plugin has: drift-corrected sync, cached Silero speech spans, the 10 ms loudness cache, Match Audio, Enhance Voice and the leveller. So the switcher is a planner over cached data that emits existing ops. Fixing the first-audio-track limit also stops silently losing the second mic.
candidates.architecture_fit: The switch is a new core op (e.g. edit_angles.rs) composing split + set_enabled on inactive angles as ONE undo step, the way insert_clip composes split + insert time. Inputs are media_speech.rs/SileroVAD.swift spans and ClipLoudness.swift, plus optional Vision mouth activity for one-mic shows. Reading every audio track means CompositionBuilder.firstTrack and core container.rs gain an audio-track index on the media or clip (format bump), with one linked clip per track at import. Split-screen comes from C5's layouts. Lifting the spec §1 multicam non-goal needs a §11 decision: narrowly for stacked tracks, or fully for a multicam clip as a nest with an angle-cut lane.
candidates.effort: M (creator-jobs, leverage: stacked tracks) to L (differentiation: multicam clip + angle grid)
competitor_refs: Riverside Editor agent layouts / in-person multicam
Final Cut Pro for iPad Live Multicam

Code: Synchronize Audio lands its alignment as move_clip and set_speed, with drift correction.

Market: YouTube reports over 1B monthly podcast viewers; Spotify says over 500M users have streamed a video podcast.

candidates.title: Camera cutout without a green screen, and camera layouts that switch mid-video
candidates.what: Tick Cut Out Person (or Remove Background) on a camera clip, and Vision segments the person on the Mac, rendered in the background like Reverse. Text Behind Subject places a title between the person and their background, using a duplicate clip with cutout on. A Layout pop-up switches the camera at the playhead, with an animated move, between corner bubble (circle or rounded), side by side, stacked for vertical, camera full and screen only. It can also frame a padded wallpaper and a rounded, shadowed window, and 'Hide camera while silent' fades the camera out during pauses using cached speech spans. Brings #124 out of the icebox.
candidates.best_rationale: Every recorder leader shipped camera cutout and layouts in Sep–Oct 2026 (Screen Studio 4, Cap 0.6, Tella, Prequel, Loom, Riverside), and every major NLE has one-click subject masking. Frame Job has chroma key and matte tracks but no ML mask, and its recorded camera sits fixed in the bottom-right corner. Leverage is high. The mask is a derived media rendered offline exactly like Reverse, voice isolation and ramp audio, and it can be placed through the existing matte-track roles with no new compositor pass. Layouts are presets over properties that actions already animate (transform, crop, corner radius, shadow). Hide-while-silent reads speech spans the app already caches.
candidates.architecture_fit: VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest (.accurate offline), with VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest for non-person subjects. The mask is rendered to an 8-bit gray HEVC (or an alpha copy) in cache/masks/ through the ReverseRenderer/ReverseCache/BackgroundRender/MediaCacheLedger pattern. First phase: the mask clip on a Luma matte track (recipe_matte.rs), with no format change. Later: a per-layer mask texture and a video.cutout key (format bump). Layouts are an action preset in the motion-presets family. Hide-while-silent uses speech_in_clip and writes opacity actions. MCP: set_video's cutout key plus a camera_layout tool. The mask timing must follow speed changes and ramps, and HLG projects need the matte in the right working space.
competitor_refs: Screen Studio 4 camera cutout + layouts + hide during silence
Final Cut Pro Magnetic Mask / Auto Mask

candidates.title: Find Clips: ranked moments from a long video that open as real vertical edits
candidates.what: Clip ▸ Find Clips… on an episode, VOD or finished edit lists 10–30 candidates of 20–60 s. Each has in and out points snapped to sentence ends, a length, a one-line reason ('laughter after the punchline', 'the clearest statement of the thesis') and a preview, with no virality score. Make Short turns checked candidates into vertical projects or versions: reframed (C3), word-captioned, cleaned of fillers, with a hook title, queued for export. Each can be reviewed as a Proposal (C12) before it lands. Ranking runs on the user's Claude key, or (per leverage and differentiation) on-device FoundationModels per chunk, with an on-device signal-only fallback when there is no key.
candidates.best_rationale: Long-to-short is what OpusClip (16M+ users), Riverside Magic Clips, Submagic, Descript Clips and Kapwing win on, all metered by credits, and Frame Job has nothing here. Cost is the biggest barrier to AI adoption (38%). Frame Job can do it locally. The cached transcript gives sentence boundaries, which answers the main Magic Clips complaint about cuts in the wrong place. The 10 ms loudness cache gives energy. Sound Analysis adds the non-verbal moments (laughter, applause, cheering) that transcript-only clippers miss. Every candidate opens as a real timeline instead of a black-box render, and every step is an MCP tool, so outside agents run the same job.
candidates.architecture_fit: SNClassifySoundRequest(.version1) on MediaCacheLane into a per-media label cache, ClipLoudness.swift peaks, and get_transcript sentence spans. Ranking is an Assistant recipe (AssistantPrompt.swift) over chunked transcripts with cached results, or a FoundationModels pass. Candidates set_range; Make Short copies the range into new_project, then set_canvas vertical, C3's reframe, detect_fillers + ripple_delete_ranges, and the existing caption pipeline. MCP: find_clips answers the ranked list. It depends on C3 and on C1's word-to-timeline mapping, and in differentiation's version also on C12 and C13.

Code: the Assistant ships no built-in creator recipes or workflows.

candidates.title: Publish kit: platform presets with rule checks, safe zones, chapter text, drafted titles and thumbnails
candidates.what: Export (or File ▸ Prepare for Publishing / Publish Kit) offers named targets: YouTube, YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Reels, Spotify video podcast and Apple Podcasts. Each sets size, codec and loudness and checks the project against that platform's published rules, with one-click fixes. View ▸ Safe Zones overlays the platform UI (labelled approximate). A Publish panel gives a copyable '00:00 Intro' chapter list built from chapter markers and checked against YouTube's rule. It drafts titles, a description and chapter names from the transcript, on-device with FoundationModels (no key) or with the user's Claude key. It also offers a thumbnail picker: suggested frames scored by Vision aesthetics, 1280×720, with a title-graphic template and three variants. Translated subtitles, which differentiation bundles here, are under C11.
candidates.best_rationale: It hits every creator on every upload and closes four inventory gaps in roughly one phase that is mostly formatting and wiring: platform presets, safe zones, chapter text, and title and description drafts. The platform rules (YouTube chapters: 00:00 first, at least 3, each at least 10 s; Spotify's video spec; Apple Podcasts loudness) are exact enough to check deterministically, which makes 'Frame Job won't let you ship a broken upload' a true claim. FoundationModels drafts give an AI tier with no key and no cost that no hosted rival can offer. Its value comes from frequency rather than from removing a hard give-up point.
candidates.architecture_fit: Presets are data rows in core export_preset.rs and ExportPresetsStore.swift. Rule checks are pure core validators kept as data with an as-of date. Chapter text is a read of add_marker {chapter} markers, the same source ExporterWriter+Chapters.swift embeds. Safe zones extend the existing 90/80% safe-area guide drawing. Drafts are a FoundationModels LanguageModelSession with @Generable output, chunked for its ~4k context, or an Assistant recipe over get_transcript. Thumbnails use Vision CalculateImageAestheticsScoresRequest feeding the existing Save Frame…, plus a bundled graphic template. MCP: a publish_kit read tool. An HLG project exported for Spotify needs the SDR version.

YouTube Studio chapters and three-thumbnail test

candidates.title: Caption design and saved styles, with a brand kit and project templates
candidates.what: Captions: an inspector Captions section exposes every word-style colour, size, background and animation as a control (today some are set only by an agent). Keyword emphasis lets the creator mark words, or have names and numbers picked by NLTagger or the Assistant, to show bigger in a highlight colour. An emoji can follow chosen words. Any caption setup or text look saves as a named style. Brand kit: brand colours and fonts appear first in every colour well and font menu and feed graphic templates' colour props by default. Final Cut Pro iPad Creator Themes
